hero.filename: Guilford Courthouse Historical Marker Greensboro North Carolina.JPG
hero.caption: North Carolina state historical marker for Guilford Courthouse, located within the boundaries of present-day Greensboro, North Carolina. Guilford Courthouse was the site of a major battle of the American Revolution, when forces under American General Nathanael Greene confronted the troops of British General Lord Cornwallis. The site of the battlefield is today a United States Military Park.

images.filename: Canary Cottage with National Votes For Women Trail Marker.jpg
images.caption: Canary Cottage served as Dr. Charlotte Hawkins Brown's home from 1925 until 1961. In front of the home today is a lavender highway marker for the National Votes for Women Trail which highlights Dr. Brown's work as a women's suffrage activist.
images.alt: Canary Cottage served as Dr. Charlotte Hawkins Brown's home from 1925 until 1961. In front of the home today is a lavender highway marker for the National Votes for Women Trail which highlights Dr. Brown's work as a women's suffrage activist.

images.caption: Modern photo of the exterior of Kimball Hall, built in 1927 it functioned as the dining hall for the Palmer Memorial Institute. Today it serves as a rental space for the Charlotte Hawkins Brown Museum.
images.alt: Modern photo of the exterior of Kimball Hall, built in 1927 it functioned as the dining hall for the Palmer Memorial Institute. Today it serves as a rental space for the Charlotte Hawkins Brown Museum.

images.caption: Modern photo of the Bell Tower. The bell tower served as the time keeper for the students of the Palmer Memorial Institute. One student was the designated bell ringer and they would go to this bell tower and ring the bell for 5 minute increments to mark transitional times for students on campus.
images.alt: Modern photo of the Bell Tower. The bell tower served as the time keeper for the students of the Palmer Memorial Institute. One student was the designated bell ringer and they would go to this bell tower and ring the bell for 5 minute increments to mark transitional times for students on campus.

images.filename: The Fountain at the Charlotte Hawkins Brown Museum.jpg
images.caption: This fountain is next to Kimball Hall on the campus of the Charlotte Hawkins Brown Museum. It was added in 2011 at the request of Palmer Memorial Institute Alumni who wanted a reflective space on campus.
images.alt: This fountain is next to Kimball Hall on the campus of the Charlotte Hawkins Brown Museum. It was added in 2011 at the request of Palmer Memorial Institute Alumni who wanted a reflective space on campus.

images.caption: Modern photo of the exterior of the Massachusetts Congregational Cottage. Built in 1949 this building provided a space for senior girls at Palmer to practice their home economics skills by living in the house for 6 weeks and running it like they would run a household. Today it is available as a rental space.
